# Milestone 4.1 — route authorization matrix

Every registered handler and every route file, classified. `tests/route-authorization.test.ts` fails if a route is
missing here, if an entry is stale, or if a handler is not mounted by a route file.

**Read the `enforcement` column as the truth.** Every row is `enforced`: there is no classified route whose
check is still to come.

Since Milestone 4.4 every route that reads one organization's records is classified `session`, and
`lib/api/next.ts` enforces it: no valid session is a 401, the permission in this table is checked against the
caller's membership role, and the read runs inside a transaction that carries the caller's organization, so
another organization's id (or an unattributed row) is a 404. Row level security (migration 0016) narrows the same
reads again inside the database.

The public surface is the **signed-only proof graph** (`/api/proof/…`): signed records anyone may re-verify in
their own browser, with nothing private added. A receipt with live provider checks, an envelope's tree, an
organization's books and its provider statement are not public.

## Categories

* **public** — Public: no private tenant data, no financial action.
* **signed-principal** — The caller signs with an Ed25519 principal whose chain is verified. No session.
* **signed-agent** — An agent's signed request is the authority. Agents never hold a human session.
* **signed-owner** — Signed by the account owner. Requires a session in the same organization from the next phase.
* **session** — Requires a validated server-side session, and enforces the permission named, for one organization.
* **webhook** — Provider-authenticated ingress. The event is a hint, never a tenant identity.
* **simulation** — Simulator only. Refused in production.
* **demo** — Demo only. Refused in production.
* **scheduler** — Internal scheduler, bearer secret. Refused in production when unconfigured.
* **operator-key** — Operator tool behind a bearer secret.

| `POST /api/organizations/invitations/:id/revoke` | session | `member.manage` | enforced | Sign-in required; member.manage. Withdraws a pending invitation of the caller's organization; one that does not exist there is a 404. |

| File | Category | Permission | Enforcement | Note |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `app/api/auth/[...auth]/route.ts` | session | — | enforced | The OIDC sign-in/callback/sign-out endpoint. Validates code, PKCE, state, nonce and issuer; creates a server-side session. |
| `app/api/health/route.ts` | public | — | enforced | Deployment and rail capabilities. No tenant data; says whether keys are sealed and not their contents. |
| `app/api/ai/status/route.ts` | public | — | enforced | Whether a model is connected. Moves no money and reads no tenant data. |
| `app/api/ai/turn/route.ts` | demo | — | enforced | A model's proposal for a demo agent; the browser turns it into signed requests and the gateway decides. |
| `app/api/ai/audit/route.ts` | demo | — | enforced | A model playing the auditor: read tools and proposals only; it cannot move money. |
| `app/api/dev/session/route.ts` | demo | — | enforced | Development sign-in for the console: refused (404) in production and when the gateway runs in the browser. It creates a real user, organization, membership and server-side session, which every later check validates. |
| `app/api/session/organization/route.ts` | session | — | enforced | Sign-in required, enforced by the route itself because it reads the session cookie rather than a signed body. Lists the organizations this person may choose between and switches the session row's active one, after an active-membership check. |
| `app/api/invitations/accept/route.ts` | session | — | enforced | Sign-in required, enforced by the route itself: the caller is signed in and has no membership in the inviting organization yet, which is the one case requestScope refuses. The token is single use, the address must match a verified email, and a GET of the link consumes nothing. |

## Compatibility of the SDK, CLI and MCP server

Everything a headless agent or the CLI sends is a **signed** request (`signed-agent`, `signed-principal`,
`signed-owner`). No session is required for those, and none was added: headless agent operation is unchanged.
The session-classified rows are the console's reads; a deployment signs people in through OIDC
(`/api/auth/signin`, `lib/auth/config.ts`), and a laptop uses the development sign-in (`app/api/dev/session`),
which is refused in production.

What the next phase adds: an organization-scoped API credential for SDK/CLI callers (running as a principal
mapped to one organization), and a session requirement layered *on top of* the existing signature for the
`signed-owner` treasury and recall routes — never instead of it.
